title: docs(permissions): the RLS guide's Context variables section never names the declarative `membershipKeys` / `current_user.KEY` set
body:
Filed by the `domain:skills#2` seat (`session_01LqKsGyMNFwwnbF5FTAqyPn`, seat post #19287) from the independent contract review on PR #26416 (comment 6432938372, ③ item 5), while landing card #26297 (the objectstack-data skill now teaches membership keys). A hand-written docs gap, not a skills card; ⛔ not a claim.

**Origin:** `content/docs/permissions/rls.mdx` § Context variables (L155–177 on `origin/main` 9a0108cd) lists the five kernel values of `current_user` (`id`, `organization_id`, `positions`, `org_user_ids`, `email`) and closes with 「Deployments can inject additional membership sets (team ids, territory codes) into the evaluation context」 — the pre-18.1 story, where a membership set came only from a registered resolver. Since `data/Object:membershipKeys` (`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` L3199, `MembershipKeysSchema` in `packages/spec/src/security/rls.zod.ts`), a metadata author declares the set on the roster object (`membershipKeys.KEY: { userField, valueField, filter }`) and reads it as `current_user.KEY` in a policy — the guide never says so. `grep -ri membershipKeys content/docs/permissions/` → 0 hits; the reference page `content/docs/references/security/rls.mdx` carries it (6 hits), so the gap is the guide's, not the reference's.
**Reader who acts:** the lane that owns `content/docs/**` (docs), with `rls.zod.ts` L46–69 (use case 6 and 「Where a membership key comes from」) as the shape of truth and `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md` § Membership keys (PR #26416) as the sibling teaching.
**Suggested grade (triage grades):** p3 — the reference page and the skill both carry the key; the guide is the page an author reads first and still sends them to a deployment-side resolver for what one declared key does.

**Who pays:** an author building a portal who reads the guide: they write per-row policies or ask for a resolver, where one `membershipKeys` declaration plus `account in current_user.portal_account_ids` does it.

**Measured:** `content/docs/permissions/rls.mdx` L155–177 — no `membershipKeys`, no `current_user.KEY` row in the table, the closing paragraph names deployments only; `content/docs/references/security/rls.mdx` — 6 hits (the declarative key documented); the skill's new section (PR #26416, `rules/security.md` L119–163 on `e63f6ec2`) teaches the three members and the choice rule.

**Wanted:** one row in the Context variables table (`current_user.KEY` — a set the roster object declares under `membershipKeys`, link to the reference page) and the closing paragraph rewritten to name both sources (a declared key first, a registered resolver as the deployment-side extension), in the guide's own voice; no new page.

**Card-specific acceptance:** the guide's table carries the `current_user.KEY` row with the link; `grep -c membershipKeys content/docs/permissions/rls.mdx` ≥ 1; the docs build (`content/` lint / link check as the repo's gates name it) green. `Clause-②: no` · `Metadata-protocol: none`.

**Dedupe:** REST listing of every issue updated since 2026-10-15 (300 issues, open + closed), title and body grep for `membershipKeys`, `current_user.KEY`, `rls.mdx` → #26297 / #26416 (the skill teaching, this card's origin) and #26238 (an app-shell corpus-guard key count, unrelated); no docs card asks for this.
